findings.evidence: Lines 14-17 vs. the theorems at lines 131-137 and 154-160, whose conclusions are about `γ ∘ φ` over `[[c,d]]` versus `γ` over `[[φ c, φ d]]`, not about the image of γ. The file's own design note (lines 26-30) concedes φ may sweep past the endpoints and back.
findings.fix: Replace with the statement actually proved: the contour integral is unchanged under precomposition with a C¹ change of parameter, the parameter interval being replaced by `[[φ c, φ d]]`.
findings.issue: Overclaim: "A contour integral `∫ t in a..b, deriv γ t • f (γ t)` depends on the curve `γ` only through its oriented image". Nothing in the file establishes image-dependence, and the claim is false — a loop traversed twice has the same oriented image but twice the integral (and twice the winding number). The file only proves invariance under precomposition with a C¹ map.

findings.fix: Drop the proof sentences from both docstrings; the module docstring already records the change-of-variables input (lines 19-22).
findings.issue: Declaration docstring describes the proof: "This is Mathlib's change-of-variables formula applied to the contour integrand `u ↦ deriv γ u • f (γ u)`." Same defect at line 206 in `IsNullHomologous.comp_reparam`: "every point outside `Ω` is automatically off the curve, so `windingNumber_comp_reparam` applies at each such point".

findings.evidence: Lines 39-49 list five results; `theorem hasDerivAt_comp_reparam` (line 81) and `theorem uIcc_endpoints_subset_image` (line 108) are public and absent.
findings.fix: Add both to the Main results list.
findings.issue: The "Main results" list omits the public `hasDerivAt_comp_reparam` (line 81) and `uIcc_endpoints_subset_image` (line 108), while listing the weaker `deriv` corollary. `uIcc_endpoints_subset_image` in particular is a reusable public lemma whose name gives no hint it lives in this file.

summary: The module docstring opens with a claim the file does not prove and which is false as stated (image-dependence of contour integrals), and two declaration docstrings describe the proof rather than the result.
